case.title: Lead change messages stay while hovered and close after 5 or 2.6 seconds
case.custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in with the "Admin" role at {Location-A}, in a browser window at least 1024 px wide.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Technicians {Technician-A} and {Technician-B} are active at {Location-A} with the "Technician" role and Time Clock on.
    For example: {Technician-A} is ZZAUTOTEST C682425 Ana and {Technician-B} is ZZAUTOTEST C682425 Ben.
  • Customer {Customer-A} has two Approved work orders, {Work-order-1} and {Work-order-2}, both led by {Technician-A}. Neither has a shift booked on the Schedule, and no line of either has its own technician or any logged time.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST C682425 Toast Timing, and {Work-order-1} and {Work-order-2} are S2-37431 and S2-37432.
  • You have a stopwatch, for example on your phone.
  • Starting screen: "Work Orders" > "All" tab, "Board View" shown, the name of {Customer-A} in "Search", no filter chosen, "Assigned to me" off.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
case.custom_steps:
1. Drag the card for {Work-order-1} from {Technician-A}'s column onto {Technician-B}'s column, let go and start the stopwatch.
  2. Keep the pointer away from the message and watch it.
  3. Drag the card for {Work-order-2} from {Technician-A}'s column onto {Technician-B}'s column and let go.
  4. Move the pointer onto the message and keep it there for 15 seconds.
  5. Move the pointer away from the message and watch it.
  6. Drag the card for {Work-order-1} from {Technician-B}'s column onto {Technician-A}'s column and let go.
  7. Click "Undo" on the message and start the stopwatch again.
  8. Keep the pointer away from the new message and watch it.
case.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: {Work-order-1} moves to {Technician-B}'s column and the message "{Work-order-1} assigned to {Technician-B}" shows, with "Undo".
  • Step 2: the message closes on its own about 5 seconds after you let go.
  • Step 3: the message "{Work-order-2} assigned to {Technician-B}" shows.
  • Step 4: the message stays open for the whole 15 seconds.
  • Step 5: the message closes on its own after you move away.
  • Step 6: {Work-order-1} moves to {Technician-A}'s column and the message "{Work-order-1} assigned to {Technician-A}" shows, with "Undo".
  • Step 7: the message closes at once, {Work-order-1} goes back to {Technician-B}'s column and a new message "Assignment undone" shows, with no "Undo" button.
  • Step 8: the "Assignment undone" message closes on its own about 2.6 seconds after it appeared.

Known problem (SV-11567, in Code Review on 28 Oct 2026, fast follow; Undo is its own ticket, Chris Ward on SV-11524, 20 Oct 2026; seen on the QA branch sv11524 on 26 Oct 2026): the message has the right words but no "Undo" button, only a close (×), and it closes after about 2.6 seconds. (1) If you see exactly that, mark this test Failed and raise nothing new. (2) If it fails in a different way, that is a new problem: report it. (3) If it behaves as the expected results say, Undo has shipped: mark it Passed and tell the QA lead.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 81 (27 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 28 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10043, story SV-10047 (Story 4, Reassign or unassign the lead technician from the board or grouped table); tickets SV-11522 (Tech View) and SV-11524 (Board View)

  • S4-R16: “The lead-change toast closes on its own after 5 seconds (5,000 ms) while it carries the Undo button, and after 2.6 seconds (2,600 ms) without one, as in the design; it stays open while the pointer is over it, and closes when Undo is clicked. The “Assignment undone” toast (S4-R32) closes after 2.6 seconds. Other success toasts dismiss automatically, as today.”
  • S4-R5: “After a successful lead change on Board View or Tech View, whether by drag, the dialog or Unassign, show the design’s toast (white, with the check icon) with an Undo button. It reads “{work order number} assigned to {technician name}”; “{work order number} lead technician set to {technician name}” when the new lead was already the technician on at least one of the work order’s lines; or “{work order number} moved to Unassigned” after removing the lead. Examples: “S1-357 assigned to Esther Howard”, “S1-702 lead technician set to Ralph Edwards”, “S1-352 moved to Unassigned”. This replaces the standard success toast for these messages only.”
  • S4-R32: “Undo puts the work order back exactly as it was before the change: the previous lead technician (or Unassigned), its previous place in that technician’s order, and any shifts the change cleared (removed shifts come back as they were; a shift that was ended at the moment of the change gets its original end time back). Each labor line goes back to the technician it had before the change, and a line that had none goes back to none; Undo does not apply the S4-R8 line rules. Undo is itself a lead change: it records its own audit entry (S4-R9), follows the Invoiced or Paid rule (S4-N2), and shows no shift-clearing prompt. After Undo the design’s toast reads “Assignment undone”, with no Undo button on it. If Undo cannot be saved, nothing changes and the alert “Couldn’t undo the change. Move the work order back by hand.” shows.”

Not yet checked against a build.
